================================================
types :: A sized bound rejects a negative length
================================================

-- The engine rejects this too:
--   Unexpected token `-`
LET $a: array<int, -3> = []

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (LetStatement
    (Keyword)
    (ParamDefinition
      (VariableName)
      (Colon)
      (Type
        (ParameterizedType
          (TypeName)
          (ERROR
            (TypeName))
          (LiteralType
            (Number
              (Int))))))
    (Array)))

==================================================
types :: A sized bound rejects a fractional length
==================================================

-- The engine rejects this too:
--   Unexpected character `.` starting float, only integers are allowed here
LET $a: array<int, 1.5> = []

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (LetStatement
    (Keyword)
    (ParamDefinition
      (VariableName)
      (Colon)
      (Type
        (ParameterizedType
          (TypeName)
          (TypeName)
          (Number
            (Int))
          (ERROR
            (Int)))))
    (Array)))

==========================================
types :: A sized bound rejects a parameter
==========================================

-- The engine rejects this too:
--   Unexpected token `a parameter`, expected an unsigned integer
-- Rejected before this change as well: the old bound was `Number`, which
-- has no parameter alternative. Pinned so the narrowing keeps it out.
LET $a: array<int, $n> = []

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (LetStatement
    (Keyword)
    (ParamDefinition
      (VariableName)
      (Colon)
      (Type
        (ParameterizedType
          (TypeName)
          (TypeName)
          (ERROR
            (VariableName)))))
    (Array)))

=============================================
types :: A sized bound rejects a float suffix
=============================================

-- The engine rejects this too:
--   Invalid token, found unexpected character `f after integer token
LET $a: array<int, 3f> = []

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (LetStatement
    (Keyword)
    (ParamDefinition
      (VariableName)
      (Colon)
      (Type
        (ParameterizedType
          (TypeName)
          (TypeName)
          (Number
            (Int))
          (ERROR))))
    (Array)))

==========================================
idioms :: A SET target rejects a parameter
==========================================

-- The engine rejects this too:
--   Unexpected token `a parameter`, expected an identifier
-- Rejected before the Idiom widening as well; pinned so widening the tail
-- never reaches the root.
CREATE t SET $x = 1

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (ERROR
    (Keyword)
    (Ident)
    (Keyword)
    (VariableName))
  (Number
    (Int)))

====================================================
types :: A LET annotation rejects the bracketed form
====================================================

-- The bracketed type is a closure-parameter spelling only. The engine
-- rejects it here:
--   Unexpected token `<`, expected a kind name
-- Unchanged from master; pinned so a refactor cannot hand the bracket back.
-- The parser recovers rather than failing outright, hence MISSING not ERROR.
LET $a: <int> = 2

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (LetStatement
    (Keyword)
    (ParamDefinition
      (VariableName)
      (Colon)
      (Type
        (ParameterizedType
          (MISSING TypeName)
          (TypeName))))
    (Number
      (Int))))

========================================================
types :: A function parameter rejects the bracketed form
========================================================

-- Same rule inside a DEFINE FUNCTION argument list:
--   Unexpected token `<`, expected a kind name
-- Unchanged from master, and recovers the same way.
DEFINE FUNCTION fn::g($x: <int>) { RETURN $x; }

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (DefineStatement
    (Keyword)
    (Keyword)
    (FunctionName)
    (ParamDefinition
      (VariableName)
      (Colon)
      (Type
        (ParameterizedType
          (MISSING TypeName)
          (TypeName))))
    (Block
      (BraceOpen)
      (ReturnStatement
        (Keyword)
        (VariableName))
      (BraceClose))))

=====================================================
types :: A sized bound's sign is joined to its digits
=====================================================

-- `+ 3` is not a literal, the same way `- 5` is not. The engine:
--   Unexpected token `+`
LET $a: array<int, + 3> = []

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (LetStatement
    (Keyword)
    (ParamDefinition
      (VariableName)
      (Colon)
      (Type
        (ParameterizedType
          (TypeName)
          (TypeName)
          (ERROR)
          (Number
            (Int)))))
    (Array)))
